**Finding: deviation (ASSIGN — high severity)**

The Agreement has no assignment heading of its own; the operative clause sits at § 10 NONASSIGNABILITY (p0042), embedded in the boilerplate run at the end of sec-7.

**What the document says:** Neither party may assign, transfer or subcontract without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

**Assessment:**
- The consent standard is mutual and reasonable — that part is fine.
- However, there is **no affiliate or successor carve-out** for Clear Capital. Every Company assignment, including an internal reorganization or a sale of the business, requires RadialSpark's consent. That falls short of even the fallback position (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice, consent only for other assignments), so it is a material failure rather than a minor wording gap.
- On the other limb, the news is good: there is **no change-of-control provision anywhere** in the Agreement (search returned nothing), and § 6 termination rights are mutual, ordinary for-convenience/for-breach rights unconnected to ownership changes. RadialSpark gains no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** a single proviso appended to § 10 that (i) lets Company assign to an affiliate or M&A successor without consent, on notice; (ii) bars Contractor from assigning to a competitor of ours; and (iii) confirms a Company change of control is not a deemed assignment and triggers no Contractor termination, suspension or re-pricing right. The mutual "not unreasonably withheld" standard is left untouched, keeping the edit minimal while reaching the preferred position.
